# `operation-added`

New operation

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `operation-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Paths and operations ([RULES.md section 2](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new operation (method + path) exists in the revision.

## Why this default

Existing clients never call it, so nothing breaks.

## Example

From test case [`operation-added`](../../test/cases/operation-added/): A new operation is info.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          '200':
            description: ok
+   '/pets/{id}':
+     get:
+       parameters:
+       - name: id
+         in: path
+         required: true
+         schema:
+           type: string
+       responses:
+         '200':
+           description: ok
```

Findings:

- `operation-added` · info · GET /pets/{id}

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  operation-added: info
```
